I examined each provided helper and judged whether it would help accomplish: “Find the customer who has the most cancelled orders in history, then compute the total spend on products in that customer’s most recent cancelled orders.” Summary judgments follow (function name -> Useful? + brief reason):

- get_dashboard_summary -> Not useful. It captures a general dashboard snapshot; the dashboard widgets don’t provide a full historical per-customer cancellation count or a reliable list of all cancelled orders needed to determine the customer with the most cancellations.

- generate_sales_summary_for_date_range -> Not useful. It changes dashboard date range and returns the dashboard text; same limitation as above (dashboard doesn’t expose full historical per-customer cancellation counts or detailed cancelled-order product totals).

- export_dashboard_snapshot -> Not useful. Similar to other dashboard helpers: exports raw dashboard text and can set store/date view, but does not provide a comprehensive orders dataset or ability to filter orders by status across history.

- extract_last_orders_csv -> Not useful. Extracts the compact “Last Orders” widget (recent orders) but that widget is limited (recent N orders) and typically omits order status granularity and full product-level totals; it cannot be used to find the customer with the most cancellations across history.

- summarize_top_search_terms_across_store_views -> Not useful. Focuses on search-term widgets, irrelevant to cancelled-order counts or spend.

- download_revenue_and_orders_report -> Not useful. Produces revenue summary and recent orders CSV from dashboard widgets. This is limited to recent/compact widgets and not the full historical orders dataset needed to find the most-cancelling customer.

- get_last_orders_csv -> Not useful. Wrapper around extract_last_orders_csv; same limitations.

- fetch_recent_orders_csv -> Not useful. Another wrapper around last-orders helpers; same limitations.

- export_orders_csv -> Not useful (for this task). Although more flexible, it exports the dashboard’s Last Orders-style table and can choose columns, it’s still scoped to the dashboard table(s) and does not navigate or export the full Sales > Orders grid with filters by status over full history. The task requires full historical cancelled-order data and ability to aggregate counts per customer.

- save_recent_orders_csv -> Not useful. Saves the last-orders CSV to disk; still limited to recent orders widget.

- export_revenue_and_orders -> Not useful. High-level wrapper that delegates to dashboard helpers; limited to dashboard widgets, not historical Sales > Orders data.

- download_last_orders_summary -> Not useful. Delegates to export_orders_csv and returns parsed recent orders; limited in scope to dashboard’s compact widget.

- download_recent_orders_csv -> Not useful. Wrapper around export_orders_csv; same limitation.

- save_last_orders_csv -> Not useful. Saves dashboard last-orders CSV; same limitation.

- export_last_orders_csv_simple -> Not useful. Simpler wrapper around export_orders_csv; still dashboard-scoped.

- export_last_orders_for_store_and_range -> Not useful. Another wrapper for dashboard last-orders; may set store/date, but still not the full historical orders dataset filtered by status.

- export_recent_orders_quick -> Not useful. Convenience wrapper for dashboard last-orders; does not provide historic cancelled-orders data.

- export_customers_csv_via_grid -> Marginally useful but not sufficient. This exports the Customers management grid (customer metadata). The exported CSV contains customer fields (ID, name, email, etc.) but does not include per-customer cancellation counts or the full orders history. It could be helpful only as a supplement (e.g., to map customer IDs/emails after you obtain order data), but by itself it cannot determine which customer has the most cancellations or compute cancelled-order product spend.

Overall conclusion: None of the provided helpers directly supply the full Sales > Orders dataset or a way to filter/export all orders by status across history, which is required to identify the customer with the most cancellations and compute product spend in their most recent cancelled orders. Therefore no helper is directly useful for completing the task end-to-end. The only marginally relevant helper is export_customers_csv_via_grid (for customer metadata), but it does not solve the core problem.
